chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said:

Dawud ibn Zurbi complained of his son to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding what he had spoiled for him. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Reform him. For what is a hundred thousand compared to what Allah has favored you with in him?'

key_terms.دَاوُدُ بْنُ زُرْبِيٍّ: Dawud ibn Zurbi, the companion who complained

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam advise when a father complained about his spoiled son?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Dawud ibn Zurbi seeks the guidance of Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) regarding his son's moral corruption. The Imam advises him to 'seek to make him good' (*istaslih*), emphasizing that the spiritual value of a righteous child far exceeds material wealth, specifically citing a hundred thousand dinars as a benchmark. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tarbiyah* (upbringing) and the prioritization of moral character over economic status in family dynamics.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said,

‘Dawood Bin Zurby complained of his son to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> regarding what he spoilt for him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Reform him. So what is a hundred thousand (compared to) what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Favoured you by him upon you’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following:

“Dawud ibn Zurbiy complained against his son before abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, because of what he had destroyed. He (the Imam) said, ‘Reform and reclaim him; a value of a hundred thousand is not important compared to the bounty that Allah has bestowed up on you.’”
